chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Count Basie's band and Herschel Evans
summary: He remembers Basie at the Savoy with Jimmy Rushing, Lester Young and Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Okay. All right. And, back to talking a little bit about the bands. What about Basie's band? What kinds of things were they doing at that time?

Oh, Basie. I remember him when he first came up. He was in the Savoy while I happened to be there too, with Jimmy Rushing. Right? Well, he, you know, he was doing something on the style of the swing/blues, like special things that he and Jimmy Rushing did together a lot. Oh, that's where you had Herschel Evans and Prez, Lester Young on tenor sax. Harris "Sweets" Edison on trumpet. And, there's another trumpet player. I know him well but I can't recall his name right now. But, he had some very good musicians
in there, and he had a good blues/swing band like "Moten Swing". That was the band that used to be Moten.
Benny Moten's band. And, the Count was one of the piano players. Benny was the piano and the Count was a piano player. And, that's the band he took over after Benny Moten passed.
But he, he had some very good musicians in there. And, I know you knew about Lester Young and Herschel Evans. Did you know about Herschel Evans?
Anything in particular you wanted to say about Herschel?
Well, in "Blue and Sentimental", he had something that reminded me of, what's the tenor player that used to be with Duke till he passed over in Europe? A big tone.
Oh, tenor player. Oh, no. I thought when you said big tone, I was thinking of Shorty Baker.

Shorty Baker I knew. I knew him. He was short, all right. But, Herschel Evans was a good tenor man with a lot of feeling. That, the tune that actually, that brought, brings back was "Blue and Sentimental". I even hum it on the record.
